title: Results and diagnosis: what do the four rows and the departures list mean for our code?
headline: The results either name a new default model or keep our three departures
setup: This is the last ticket: a conversation with the owner once the battles are done. Three rows are battled for sure, and a fourth only if its check says so. A linear row that wins becomes the candidate to replace the default model. If no row wins, our three tested departures from the papers stay as ours.
alt: Each battled row gets a verdict at guidance 2, 4 and 8. A linear row that wins at two or more of them, and loses at none, becomes the candidate to replace the default model. A win under 0.002 is treated as training luck and can earn a second training seed. If no row wins, the three tested departures stay as ours.
terms: A place where our code differs from the papers MD4 and LLaDA. Three are tested here: the masking rate, the decoding order and the t told while sampling
One way to train and sample the model. Four are compared. The control is Per-field, uncorrected t: our own settings
The model every run uses unless it names another. Today it is a per-field model trained on an older table
How hard the sampler pushes toward the win rate asked for. 1 is no push, and higher pushes harder
The gap two trainings of one recipe show by chance alone: up to 0.0019 in error. A win under 0.002 is treated as luck
One win among the three guidance values. It does not make a row a candidate
